title: Freezing Cancer Cell Lines
author: Emily Souster
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgtyjwpw

steps.title: Prepare freezing media
steps.instruction: Make freezing media by mixing complete culture medium with 10% (v/v) DMSO, preparing 1 mL per cryovial.

steps.title: Detach and collect cells
steps.instruction: Detach adherent cancer cells from the flask following Steps 1‑6 of the standard passaging protocol, then collect the cells.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant and resuspend
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet, then resuspend the pellet in the calculated volume of freezing media (e.g., 5 mL for 5 vials from a T150) and mix thoroughly to obtain a single‑cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in appropriate volume of freezing media
Mix well to achieve a single‑cell suspension

steps.title: Aliquot cells into cryovials
steps.instruction: Dispense 1 mL of the cell suspension into each pre‑labelled 1.8 mL cryovial.

steps.title: Freeze vials at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Place the cryovials in a CoolCell or equivalent controlled‑rate freezing container and store at –80 °C overnight; the container should achieve a cooling rate of approximately –1 °C per minute.

steps.title: Transfer to liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Move the frozen vials from –80 °C to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage.
